They are entry points into the append-only ledger in `migration_ledger.go`, not golden outputs generated by current code and not examples tied to one migration incident.

The files historically named `application-disabled` and `application-gcs` prove real startup writer profiles, but they are not complete application-state corpora. Treating them as semantic migration coverage allowed the `007 -> 008` implementation to list the obsolete `state/` namespace while real schema-007 authority lived behind `state-indexes/` and `state-versions/`. The complete fixtures added from v0.3.2 onward include profile, account, credential index and credential, session, administrator role, invite, recovery, share, preference, operation and ceremony authority plus a virtual-authenticator oracle. Qualification must recover those exact values and complete a real signed passkey assertion; merely opening the engine, listing files, or decoding one record is not semantic evidence.

The releases in a validity range have identical durable writer and canonical-format source blobs for the represented epoch. For v0.1.0–v0.1.4, `format.go`, `transfers.go`, and `engine.go` are respectively Git blobs `422e0df8c13fb4e041d7d9065ad9826079d7b541`, `c95e7035d2b72b896e09101e38268a4b1c7d2805`, and `0eea6130ec29c918c22c0f14e83f4c8f28bf9770`. For schema 003 they are `423ae18d348a78181eb250214e90bea17d0ce532`, `f3165e5b04a8b5cf44c3778f9b734e5f3e1ea409`, and `0d023e455d51ec0050c90354ef9a44ad6654faab`. Schema 001's gate has no `writerFeatures` field; this unbound representation is part of the historical epoch even when the writer set carries application capabilities. The v0.1.7 interrupted fixture captures that predecessor closing the unbound gate under `automatic-recursive-byte-aggregates-v1` and then failing on the historical upload encoding. The production release ranges and linear edges live in `migration_ledger.go`; the executable fixture/profile registry and immutable digests live in `schema_migration_test.go`.

Do not edit or regenerate an existing fixture. When a change creates a new durable schema:

1. demonstrate the current binary fails against the preceding epoch fixture;
2. append exactly one schema definition carrying its adjacent transformation from the preceding epoch, then append the new epoch's first-release boundary when applicable;
3. enumerate every durable application writer profile for that release and generate representative live, trash, zero-byte, empty-directory, completed-upload, and aborted-upload state for each profile using code that writes the new epoch;
4. export raw backend key/body maps without current-code decoding or rewriting;
5. record the source tag or commit and SHA-256 digest here and in the executable registry;
6. run each predecessor binary through every durable boundary it can publish, preserve exact interrupted/failed residue as additional immutable fixtures, and prove every epoch/profile/interruption fixture traverses the complete remaining ledger suffix in single- and split-backend modes;
7. construct every profile through the real application startup writer builder and prove restart at every durable edge boundary plus concurrent multi-replica convergence;
8. add a predecessor-produced complete application corpus with a semantic oracle for every authoritative feature family, prove actual cryptographic authentication and a new mutation after the full suffix, and prove conflicts, missing sources, corrupt proofs, crashes, and two-to-eight-replica convergence fail or recover as specified;
9. run `nix run .#test-migration -- vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and `nix flake check`.

Epoch definitions, adjacent transformations, release ranges, fixture associations, and fixture bytes are append-only. Removing or rewriting one requires the major-version compatibility process in `AGENTS.md` and the normative specification.
